title: Why the Best Players Look Slow
logline: The next night on the same floodlit pitch, a young player's friend Sam passes the balls in while Chalk, the keeper made of pitch paint, chases instead of guarding. The first pass bounces off a stiff foot and is gone in two seconds: where did the time go? A glowing ring shows the answer, the seconds until Chalk reaches the ball, and three chapters buy more of it: look before the ball arrives, cushion the first touch into space, and receive half-turned on the back foot. The same pass at the end reads four times the time. Same legs, same speed: that is why the best players look slow.

characters.name: Tavi (the player, spoken to only as 'you')
characters.design: As episode 1: teal shirt, orange chest band, dark shorts, chalk-white boots, warm brown skin, cloud-tuft hair, rounded shapes, no outlines. New this episode: headTurn 0..1 for scans (about 12 frames out and back), the receive pose family (receiveReady, receiveSoft, receiveStiff, lookBack, passInside) and a side-on stance hinted with a small body twist. Faces: focus when scanning, wince on the stiff-foot bounce, happy at the end. In the map view: TopPlayer kind 'tavi' with facing, look and a VisionFan.
characters.role: The viewer's stand-in. Never named in narration. Faces Sam straight on in the cold open, meets the pass with a locked foot and loses the ball in two seconds. Learns to look, touch and shape, then replays the first pass with two scans, a jog to meet the ball, a half-turn and a back-foot cushion into space.

characters.name: Sam (the friend, the passer)
characters.design: Player with colors SAM_COLORS from the kit: orange shirt, no chest band, lighter skin, short dark hair, same build as Tavi. Calm, always the passer. Carries a net bag of balls in the cold open. In the map view: TopPlayer kind 'sam'. Side view: stands left and passes with passInside.
characters.role: Feeds every pass from behind Tavi (Tavi's back to the goal). Calls a cone colour in the LOOK drill and a gate in the SHAPE drill. Never speaks in narration; two speech bubbles in practice ('WHITE!', 'LEFT!'). Moves left after the ending pass to receive Tavi's calm second touch.

characters.name: Chalk (the keeper made of pitch paint, now chasing)
characters.design: As episode 1: capsule body of chalk white, mitten gloves, dot eyes and eyebrow dashes, chalk dust at every step. New: runA/runB chasing cycle with flip on, puffed pose when he arrives late, a small wave and two blinking dot eyes from the dark half of the map, a grey blob variant for the blurry side-vision beats, a cone stand-in with one eyebrow in the wall drill. Never speaks. One eyebrow when beaten, two after the fake.
characters.role: The deadpan problem-setter, out of the goal all night. He always jogs at 4 m/s from the same mark, 11 m on the goal side of Tavi, starting on the kick frame, so the only thing that changes between the cold open and the ending is Tavi. Steals the ball in the cold open (skids past, turns, pokes it away at about two seconds) and arrives to nothing at the end.

characters.name: The Time Bubble (motif)
characters.design: TimeBubble ring around Tavi with a mono seconds readout: distance to Chalk divided by his jog of 4 m/s (secondsToReach, CLOSING_SPEED). Pink under 0.5 s with an alarm pulse, amber near 1 s, lime from 2 s. Squashed in side views, round in the map. Planted with 'Remember this ring' in b02; a grey sprint ghost ring in b02 shows that a faster Chalk shrinks the numbers, not the fixes.
characters.role: The honest scoreboard of the episode. Reads 0.6 s in the cold open and 2.4 s in the ending. Each chapter ends with it growing or being used as the skill is applied: 1.0 s after LOOK's early step, 0.7 s against 0.2 s after TOUCH's touch away, and after SHAPE's half-turn 1.0 s at the ready frame against 0.4 s for the straight-on receiver, who is only ready after her turn. Chalk's jog never changes with Tavi's stance, so the ring never 'holds'; skills change when Tavi is ready and where the ball is. Every reading comes from a distance in the sims; it never uses top speed.

characters.name: Snapshots and the map in your head (motif)
characters.design: Snapshot polaroids pop with a camera-flash frame on every scan (tick) and fly into a ThoughtBubble over Tavi's head. Before scanning the bubble shows UnknownFog question marks; after two scans it is a tiny top-down map with Chalk's dot and arrow and a lime patch of space. A small lime eye icon marks 'eyes on the ball' after the second look.
characters.role: Shows that a scan is a snapshot, not a stare, and that two looks (kick frame and halfway) build the picture before the ball arrives, with the eyes back on the ball for the touch. Pays off in the ending when the two snapshots match and the ring is already there before the ball is, and in the last line ('take a snapshot').

learn_words.meaning: a quick look over your shoulder, away from the ball, to see where the defender and the space are, then back
your first contact with a pass, and where it sends the ball

scenes.narration: The next night. <short pause> Your friend Sam's on passing duty. <short pause> Chalk's out of goal, chasing. <short pause> Your back's to the goal. You face Sam. The pass comes. <short pause> Stiff foot. It bounces away. You look up. <long pause> Chalk's already there. Ball gone. <short pause> You had the ball for two seconds. It felt like nothing. Where did the time go?
visual_beats: [1 s silent pre-roll] Same dark sky and star field as s01. The four floodlights clunk on one after another, each blooming its glow rings. The StandClock reads nine (hours 21).
'The next night.' Slow push (8% over 5 s) past the stand. A chalk caption on the grass: 'NIGHT 2'. Dust drifts in the beams. The goal line lies flat and empty: no keeper in it.

'Your friend Sam's on passing duty.' Sam (Player, colors SAM_COLORS: orange shirt, no band) jogs in from the left with a net bag of balls and tips them out. Two small sim bounces per ball. Label 'SAM' pops. He taps one ball forward with the inside of the foot (passInside).

'Chalk's out of goal, chasing.' The goal-line paint peels up and builds Chalk, as in s01, but he steps OFF the line (flip on) and jogs to a spot 11 m on the goal side of Tavi's mark. He mimes two quick run steps (runA/runB) and a dust puff. Label 'CHALK' pops, one eyebrow lift, then eyebrows down: business.
'Your back's to the goal.' Tavi walks to the mark 12 m in front of Sam. A faint chalk arrow from her back to the goal, far right.
'You face Sam.' She stands square to him (flip on, facing left). Wide side view settles: Sam left, Tavi centre, Chalk far right.

'The pass comes.' PASS_IN: Sam side-foots the ball along the grass. Chalk starts jogging the moment the ball leaves Sam's foot (CHALK_CHASE). Tavi's eyes follow the ball only (receiveReady, face neutral).
'Stiff foot.' STIFF_BOUNCE: the ball reaches Tavi at about 4.8 m/s and meets a locked, still foot and ankle (receiveStiff). Squash on contact. Face wince.
'It bounces away.' The ball rebounds at about 1.6 m/s back toward Sam and a little left, short trail. Tavi turns after it and stops it dead under the sole about a metre away.
'You look up.' Only now her head lifts and turns toward the goal side (headTurn). Face focus. Chalk's shadow slides in from the right. Whoosh.
[long pause] Camera pushes 10% toward Tavi. Chalk skids past her mark, stops, turns.
'Chalk's already there.' He jogs the last two metres, pokes the ball away with a mitten and stands over it. One eyebrow up.
'Ball gone.' The ball rolls out of frame right. Tavi's shoulders drop (shrug pose, half).
'You had the ball for two seconds.' A chalk stopwatch Readout pops above Tavi: it fills 0.0 to 2.0 s while the last two seconds replay as a faint ghost overlay.
'It felt like nothing.' The stopwatch face turns pink and the hands spin away to nothing.
'Where did the time go?' Everything dims 30% except Tavi and the empty grass where the ball was. A chalk '?' is written at her feet.

CHALK_CHASE: Chalk starts at (10.9, -1.5), 11.0 m from Tavi, and jogs at 4 m/s toward her from the kick frame; at the arrival frame he is 2.5 m away. STIFF_BOUNCE: firstTouch with ballVel (4.8, 0, 0), footVel 0, normal (-0.95, 0.31, 0), e 0.35 (a real foot's limited mass, not the kit's heavy-foot 0.6), grip 0.8: the ball leaves at 1.62 m/s toward (-0.88, 0.48), 34% of the pass speed, and would roll 1.65 m. Tavi stops it dead at about +1.1 s, 1.3 m from her mark near (-1.14, 0.62), and looks up at about +1.4 s. Chalk reaches her old mark at +0.63 s, overruns about a metre and stops (+0.9 s), turns (+1.3 s), jogs about 2.2 m back to the ball (+1.85 s) and pokes it away at about +2.0 s after the ball first touched her.

facts_used: 'two seconds' is sim time: the ball first touches Tavi at t = 2.12 s and Chalk pokes it away about 2.0 s later (STIFF_BOUNCE plus CHALK_CHASE with the overrun, stop and turn). Pros hold the ball about 1.1 s per possession (Ligue 1), so two seconds is generous, and it still feels like nothing.
Chalk's 4 m/s jog is the episode's CLOSING_SPEED (challenge tweak 3: a jog is more honest than top speed; youth top speeds are about 6.3-7.4 m/s).

The stiff-foot rebound of about a third <- verification: a still firm foot returns about 20-40% of the pass speed. Sim gives 34%. The mistake is a locked foot and ankle, not a shin: a rolling pass meets the foot.

'if he keeps coming at a jog' states the closing-speed assumption once in plain words (EP2-VISUAL: never use top speed). 4 m/s is below youth top sprint speeds (about 6.3 m/s at U12, 7.4 m/s at U16, general boys). 'Sprinting shrinks the numbers, not the fixes' answers the viewer who knows real defenders sprint: the three skills work at any closing speed, only the readings change.
'One heartbeat' is a comparison: a resting heartbeat lasts about 0.6-1.0 s (general knowledge, no number spoken).

scenes.chapter: Ch1 Look: what a scan is
scenes.narration: Way one: look. <short pause> Before the ball comes, look over your shoulder. You know this one: a scan. <short pause> A snapshot, not a stare. Click, and back. Your eyes barely stop. <short pause> One question: where's Chalk? <short pause> Pros do it right up to the touch.
visual_beats: [1 s card] Chalk writes '1 · LOOK' on the grass, subtitle 'buy time before the ball'. The card's ring icon is lime.
'Way one: look.' Side view. Tavi waits for a pass from Sam. Her head turns over her shoulder toward the goal side (headTurn 0 to 1 and back over about 12 frames). Face focus.

'Before the ball comes, look over your shoulder.' SlowMoTag. The head turn replays at 1/4 speed with a thin arc Arrow from the ball to over the shoulder. A stopwatch Readout beside her head counts 0.00 to 0.40 s. Caption under it: 'pro midfielders, Norway'.

'You know this one: a scan.' WordCard: scan, a quick look over your shoulder, away from the ball, to see where the defender and the space are, then back. The card pops with a small 'yes, that one' nod from Tavi.
'A snapshot, not a stare.' A Snapshot polaroid pops out of her head with a camera-flash frame: Chalk far away, the free grass, the goal. It tilts and hangs in the air.
'Click, and back.' Tick. Her head is already back on the ball before the polaroid stops wobbling.
'Your eyes barely stop.' Close inset of her eyes: they sweep across during the turn with almost no hold, a faint blur streak.
'One question: where's Chalk?' The polaroid zooms: a chalk circle draws around Chalk's tiny figure in it. Label 'CHALK' with a distance tick. The rest of the polaroid stays soft.

'Pros do it right up to the touch.' Cut to the map. A grey ghost pro token waits above a 10 s chalk timeline. Three polaroids pop along it, about one every three seconds. The pass leaves at about 8 s and arrives at 10 s, so the last look lands while the ball rolls. Caption: 'Premier League pros: about 3 looks in the 10 s before the ball'.
scenes.physics_sim: Map beat: a 10 s timeline; DRILL_PASSES 8 m at 5 m/s, decel 0.8, leaves at 8.1 s and arrives at 10 s (1.9 s roll); polaroids at about 1, 4 and 8.5 s. Head turn: 12 frames out and back at real speed (0.4 s).
sfx: soft cloth turn of the head
three ticks spaced along the timeline
scenes.transition_out: The last polaroid flips over. Its back is the X-ray grid, and the camera pushes into it.
facts_used: Stopwatch 0.40 s (visual, captioned 'pro midfielders, Norway') <- 'Pros (4 Norwegian top-league central midfielders, eye-tracking): an average scan lasts 0.40 s; nine out of ten last 0.66 s or less; only 2.3% of scans contain a fixation.' The caption names Norway so viewers do not merge this group with the Premier League group.

'Your eyes barely stop' <- the same source (mechanism note: do not say the eyes stop; 97.7% of scans hold no fixation, and the topic 3 note asks for 'almost never stop', so 'barely' replaces 'don't even').

Caption 'Premier League pros: about 3 looks in the 10 s before the ball' <- 'Premier League pros (27 players, 9,574 possessions) scan about 3 times in the 10 seconds before the ball arrives'. The timeline shows the same rate as the caption (about one look every three seconds), and the last look during the roll follows the semi-elite adult finding that head turns rise in the final second before the ball. No spoken number here.

scenes.narration: Why not look after it arrives? <short pause> Noticing something new: about a third of a second. Choosing what to do: about half a second. <short pause> That's two of Chalk's steps. <short pause> Like checking for cars after stepping off the kerb. <short pause> Check first. Then move.
visual_beats: 'Why not look after it arrives?' X-ray grid. XRayHead: Tavi's head in profile with the eye and a simple brain outline in teal ink. The ball arrives at her foot at the bottom of frame. Only then does the head turn.

'Noticing something new: about a third of a second.' TwoPartStopwatch, part one 'NOTICE' fills from 0 to about 0.3 s while a pulse travels from the eye into the brain. Caption: 'ages 10 to 18, computer tests'.

'Choosing what to do: about half a second.' Part two 'CHOOSE' fills to about 0.5 s while two glowing doors (turn, pass) blink in the brain and one lights up. The two dials sit side by side, not summed.

'That's two of Chalk's steps.' Below the head, a chalk Chalk jogs across the grid along a short SecondsRuler: two chalk footprints appear one metre apart in exactly 0.5 s of dial time. His mitten comes to rest on the ball. One eyebrow up.

'Like checking for cars after stepping off the kerb.' ChalkSketch kerb: a small chalk kid steps off a kerb, THEN turns their head. A chalk car's headlights swing in with a honk. Pink MISTAKE stamp on the sketch.
'Check first.' The sketch rewinds: the head turns first, the kid waits on the kerb. The car passes.
'Then move.' The kid crosses cleanly. Teal FIX stamp. Both dials collapse to zero: nothing left to do when the ball comes.

Inset: a side view of Tavi with an arm out and a thumb up; a small lime circle sits on the thumbnail. Inset caption: 'sharp spot: about 5 degrees; a thumbnail at arm's length fits inside it'.
'The rest: blur.' Outside the wedge, the fan goes soft and grainy.

'It catches movement, not whose shirt.' In the dim fan, Chalk's token jogs across at the edge: a blurry grey blob that pings like radar when he moves. Sam's token stands still in the dim fan: also a grey blob. Two chalk shirts float in the dim zone, one teal, one white, both drawn grey. The sharp wedge swings onto one and it turns white: Chalk.

facts_used: 'A bit more than a half circle' <- 'Humans see about 200-220 degrees horizontally with both eyes, a bit more than a half circle; the sharp centre is only about 5 degrees' and the challenge (tweak 5): 'about a half circle is a safe under-claim'. VisionFan wideDeg 200 is drawn just past the hands and stays under the verified 214 degrees. The arms-out picture <- research metaphor 'hold your arms straight out to the sides'.

scenes.chapter: Ch3 Shape: straight on costs a turn
scenes.narration: Face Sam straight on. Goal behind you. Chalk lives there. <short pause> To play forward, you turn. A full turn costs over half a second. Timed on youth players running and turning, no ball. <short pause> That's your whole ring from the first pass.
visual_beats: 'Face Sam straight on.' Map view. Tavi's token faces Sam, chest to the ball. Her wide fan covers Sam and the sides.
'Goal behind you.' The goal end behind her is drawn dark. A small chalk goal icon sits in the dark.
'Chalk lives there.' Chalk's two dot eyes blink open in the dark half, then his token gives a small wave. Blip.
'To play forward, you turn.' The ball arrives on her front foot. Her token rotates a full half circle with the ball at its feet. A stopwatch Readout runs beside her.

'A full turn costs over half a second.' The stopwatch stops at about 0.6 s. While she turned, Chalk's token took two steps and two chalk footprints appear on a short SecondsRuler, 2 m closer. Her ring shrinks from 1.0 s to 0.4 s and goes pink.

'Timed on youth players running and turning, no ball.' Caption: 'run-and-turn test, boys 11 to 15, no ball'. A small inset shows the test: 5 m out, turn, 5 m back, against a straight 10 m run. A chalk 'about' tag hangs on the stopwatch.
'That's your whole ring from the first pass.' The b02 pink ring '0.6 s' pops beside the stopwatch, same size. They match. Blip.

The turn cost 0.56-0.66 s.' scenes.narration: Now stand side-on. The half-turn. Old cue, new reason. <short pause> Sam in the corner of one eye, the goal in the other. <short pause> The corner of your eye catches movement. The look tells you who. <short pause> Every look is now a small turn.

'Every look is now a small turn.' A chalk arc above her head compares the two head turns: a long arc from the straight-on stance, a short arc from the side-on stance. The short arc glows.

scenes.narration: Take it on your back foot, the one further from Sam. Toes where you're going. <short pause> It rolls across you, train through a station. <short pause> Half-turned, back foot: no turn to pay for. You play forward while the ring's still big.

Her far foot glows lime, Label 'back foot' points at it; a faint 'near foot' label on the other. WordCard: back foot, the foot further from the passer, not the foot behind you.
'Toes where you're going.' A lime Arrow draws from the toes of the far foot toward the goal side: the foot is open, toes pointing where the touch will go, not at Sam.

'It rolls across you, train through a station.' PASS_IN's last metres. The ball passes the near foot and reaches the far foot, slow motion for the last half metre. ChalkSketch train: a chalk train (the ball with a chimney) rolls into a station shaped like her two feet, past the first platform (near foot) and out the far side (back foot). Whistle. Cushion on the back foot (receiveSoft, footTurn): the ball rolls about 1.3 m ahead of her, on the goal side, along the lime arrow.
'Half-turned, back foot: no turn to pay for.' A stopwatch Readout beside her stays at 0.00. Cut to the map: the same receive from above. Her token does not rotate; her chest already points forward.

'You play forward while the ring's still big.' SplitCompare on the map. Each half freezes at its READY frame: the half-turned receiver at the touch, ring 1.0 s amber, Label 'ready'; the straight-on receiver at the end of her turn, ring 0.4 s pink, Label 'ready'. Stamp CUE: 'side-on, back foot'.

Meaning 'the foot further from the passer, not the foot behind you' <- research misconception 'Back foot means the foot at the back. It means the foot farther from the passer.' The short spoken definition stays for U12 viewers because of that misconception.
'Toes where you're going' <- the BACK_FOOT normal (-0.5, 0.87): the inside of the far foot faces the goal side, so the ball goes forward; toes at Sam would send it back to him.

'no turn to pay for. You play forward while the ring's still big' <- the ring rule: Chalk closes at 4 m/s whatever Tavi does, so the half-turn does not hold the ring; it removes the 0.6 s turn (SHAPE_TURN), so she is ready at 1.0 s instead of 0.4 s. The SplitCompare freezes each receiver at her ready frame so the picture matches the rule.

scenes.narration: Classic mistake: facing the passer with room to turn. <short pause> Fix: side-on, before the pass. <short pause> Two gates behind you. Sam calls a gate, then passes. Open to that gate. Back foot, one touch through it, pass back. <short pause> Easy passes first.
visual_beats: 'Classic mistake: facing the passer with room to turn.' PracticeBoard with three cues: 'Chest between passer and goal', 'Let it run to the back foot, toes open', 'Look while it travels'. Stamp MISTAKE. Left panel, map: Tavi's token faces Sam, chest to the ball, dark half behind her, lime space open behind her. Chalk's token waves from the dark, far away. Board note: 'Snapshot says room behind? Half-turn. Chalk on your back? Stay straight on, keep your body between him and the ball, pass back.'
'Fix: side-on, before the pass.' Stamp FIX. Her token steps and turns a quarter before Sam's pass leaves. The fan now reaches both Sam and the goal.
'Two gates behind you.' Stamp DRILL. Right panel, map: Sam 10 m from Tavi. Two flat-marker gates 2 m wide pop 3 m behind her, left and right, 2 m either side of her line.
'Sam calls a gate, then passes.' A Bubble from Sam says 'LEFT!' BEFORE his foot moves. Tavi's look flicks to find the left gate (tick).
'Open to that gate.' Her token turns a quarter toward the left gate while the ball is still at Sam's foot. Then the pass leaves.

'Back foot, one touch through it, pass back.' Her token receives side-on on the far foot, one touch sends the ball through the left gate, she follows and passes back to Sam. Board note: 'Ten each way, then swap. Level 2: Sam calls as the ball leaves. Look, then open. No friend? Wall: pass side-on, take the rebound on the back foot, turn out in one touch.'

'Easy passes first.' Board line: 'Easy passes first. Add pace when every touch goes through the gate. Swap roles often.' Safety line on the board: 'Flat markers, not tall cones. Keep the lane behind the gates clear. No tackles.' The board's ring icon pops to lime: 'the turn is already done'.

Gate touch: redirect at 2.5 m/s toward the called gate, 3 m behind and 2 m to the side (gate centre 3.6 m away); rollDistance(2.5) = 3.9 m, so the ball rolls through the gate and stops just past it, where she takes the second touch and passes back.

facts_used: No narrated numbers. Drill <- research 'Three-gate receiving (needs one friend)' and 'Half-turn gate (pair)', trimmed to two gates, and the challenge's drill (c): receive through a gate on the half-turn and play forward in two touches. The gate is called BEFORE the pass so the receiver can open before the ball leaves, as the fix says; level 2 on the board calls it on the kick. Gates at 3.6 m so a 2.5 m/s first touch (3.9 m) really goes through in one touch and stays near the 'two metres, not zero' band. The wall variant <- 'Half-turn wall drill (alone)'.

'with room to turn' <- the half-turn is not always right: with a marker tight on the back, opening exposes the ball (research: protect the ball with the body, FA ages 7-11). The board note links the choice to the chapter 1 snapshot.
Safety lines from the same drills (flat markers, clear lane, easy passes first, no tackles) live on the board, not in the narration.

scenes.narration: One more way: steal time. <short pause> Shoulders one way, ball the other. <short pause> One test, adult players: a fake cost the defender about half a second. Two of Chalk's steps, stolen. <short pause> But that's for another night.

'But that's for another night.' The chalk card's '?' stays; the rest of the card rubs itself out. The music drops to the ending pad.

Chalk, 3 m away at 4 m/s, leans left for the 0.5 s readout, then has to reverse: he reaches the ball's new spot about 1 s after it left, by which time Tavi has taken it on. scenes.narration: Back foot. It rolls across you. <short pause> Soft touch, into space. Away from Chalk. <short pause> Read the ring. Almost two and a half seconds. <long pause> Chalk arrives. <short pause> To nothing.

facts_used: 'Four times the time' <- the two sim readings, 0.63 s and 2.39 s (ratio 3.8, 'about four times' as the concept states: 'Cold open: 0.6 s. Ending: the same pass, 2.4 s').

'You looked earlier, moved earlier' says where the time came from: at the touch frame the ring reads 2.4 s because Tavi met the ball 4 m early (Chalk 9.6 m away, ENDING_RUN), and the early move was possible because the first look found Chalk. 'Same speed' is honest for Tavi's legs: her jog in the ending (3.5 m/s) is below youth top speeds and no faster than her chase after the bouncing ball in the cold open. visual_beats: 'Where did the time go?' The chalk '?' from b01 is written on the grass again at her feet.
'Nowhere.' The '?' rubs itself out. In its place, the ring is drawn on the grass in chalk, lime.

'You bought it before anyone noticed.' ChalkSketch coins: three small chalk coins of time drop into the grass ring, as in b03. Chalk, still puffed, sinks back into the goal line, which lies flat again, one eyebrow last to go. Sam waves and jogs off with the bag of balls.
'Lights out.' The StandClock reads half past nine. The floodlights clunk off one by one, the reverse of b01. A last pool of light stays on the chalk ring in the grass.
'Next pass that rolls at you: take a snapshot.' In the last pool of light Tavi walks off, turns her head once over her shoulder. Camera click. A polaroid drifts up into the dark.

[2.5 s hold] The ring glows once. The camera pulls back to the dark stadium as one warm dot among the city lights. End card: 'WHY THE BEST PLAYERS LOOK SLOW' in chalk letters, then a fade to the night-sky colour.
